purpose: Harness smoke observations (fake loopback model, hidden consoles, no approval answered). Not live-trial evidence.

findings.summary: Codex 0.164.0 runs hook commands through PowerShell 7 on this machine; the generated cmd-style hook string is a PowerShell parse error and delivered no capture; the PowerShell call form delivered the events.
findings.probe: echo %COMSPEC% $PSHOME written by a hook printed the literal %COMSPEC% and the expanded PSHOME; ingress with the quoted-path-first string wrote 0 captures in two TUI runs (sync and async) while the PowerShell call form wrote 4.
findings.status: unverified for the user's real Codex configuration

findings.summary: Async Codex hook registration let PermissionRequest reach the ingress before PreToolUse (ingress-only ordering, about 20 ms apart); the request was treated as resolved and no wait was shown.
findings.status: observed once in the managed-runtime harness run; needs confirmation

findings.summary: Claude 2.1.310 in auto mode emitted no PermissionRequest and no Notification while the classifier call was pending, so a slow automatic approval cannot reach Bell Tower's provisional path through the real mechanism.
findings.status: observed in the TUI with the fake classifier endpoint

findings.summary: A PermissionRequest hook that holds longer than about 6 s still produced Notification permission_prompt, so Bell Tower confirmed and announced although no person was asked.
findings.status: observed for the hook-delay mechanism only; not Claude's automatic reviewer

limitations: Bell Tower 0.1.9012 writes no announcement log; announcement eligibility is derived from persisted state using the product's AlertPolicy rule, chips are read through UI Automation.
The visible-window launch path and a real-display screenshot of the second tray were not exercised.
